Round 2 sent every line of numerics code back through both referees. Verdicts split — Gemini passed the revised docs (SOUND) while GPT-5.6 failed them pending precision fixes; on the code, both found real bugs and Gemini manufactured one:

Round-2 findingRefereeAdjudication
Poisson solve carried a spurious s²=16 scale — the OT seed's ray map was mis-scaledboth accepted fixed; seed now converges 2.2× faster, 61 vs 246 vortices
"LZ exponent off by factor 16" in the survival modelGemini refuted depth-convention mismatch; the formula is validated by the 24-point sweep against his own solver
Cubic campaign is separable — the general projection law was never actually testedGPT-5.6 accepted new nonseparable campaign: the law is leading-order only (+2–32% excess loss), and corner factorization breaks (+0.01–0.18) exactly where separability fails — see Figure 9
MRAF mixing parameter declared but never usedboth accepted true mixing implemented; honest result: comparable fidelity, 5.8× efficiency for the OT seed
Noise model was RIN, not shot noise; single random baseline; metric off-by-ones; min-norm rank test; missing |·|; stale commentsboth accepted all fixed; Poisson noise + 5-seed baselines + rational- subset rank test; all verdicts and headline results survived re-measurement
Ramp "0.28% is internally inconsistent (should be ~1.1%)"GPT-5.6 partly their estimate used the window-average speed; at the measured minimum crossing speed the incoherent estimate is 0.37% vs 0.28% measured (mild coherent assist). Claim renamed "loss-reducing," conservative 90×, stable under resolution doubling

Scorecard across both rounds: 2 referee findings refuted by direct measurement, ~20 accepted and fixed, and the single most valuable outcome — the nonseparable campaign — exists only because a referee demanded it. Both manuscripts and all figures reflect post-review numbers.
